paragraphs.title: Preparing the Offerings and Unleavened Bread

easy.question: Which animals are commanded in the first verse?
answers: One bull and two rams
Two bulls and one ram
One lamb and two goats
easy.explanation: The verse commands one young bull and two rams.

easy.question: What kind of bread is mentioned in the second verse?
answers: Leavened bread
Unleavened bread
Barley bread
easy.explanation: The verse mentions unleavened bread, cakes, and wafers.

easy.question: What should the bread be placed in?
answers: A table
An altar
One basket
easy.explanation: The third verse says to put them in one basket.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Prepare the bread, place it in a basket, and bring it with the animals
Offer the animals, then prepare the bread
Place the animals in a basket, then bake the bread
medium.explanation: The bread is prepared first, then placed in a basket and brought with the animals.

medium.question: What does “without blemish” mean in this context?
answers: Very large
Whole and free from defects
Especially young
medium.explanation: The rams had to be complete and without defects.

medium.question: How is oil used in the bread?
answers: Only to cook the bull
It is poured over the basket afterward
The cakes are mixed with oil and the wafers are anointed with oil
medium.explanation: The cakes are made with oil, while the wafers are anointed with oil.

challenge.question: What detail distinguishes the number of bulls from the number of rams?
answers: There is one bull and two rams
There are two bulls and one ram
There are equal numbers of bulls and rams
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies one bull and two rams.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from placing the bread in a basket while mentioning the animals separately?
answers: Only the animals are in the basket
The basket is for the bread, while the animals are brought separately
The bread may not be brought with the animals
challenge.explanation: The bread is put in the basket, and the bull and rams are mentioned separately.

challenge.question: What is the purpose of the preparations at the beginning of the first verse?
answers: To prepare an ordinary meal
To teach people how to raise cattle
To consecrate those appointed to minister to the Lord
challenge.explanation: The preparations are for hallowing them to serve the Lord.

questions.question: What detail distinguishes the number of bulls from the number of rams?
answers: There is one bull and two rams
There are two bulls and one ram
There are equal numbers of bulls and rams
questions.explanation: The verse specifies one bull and two rams.

questions.question: What can be inferred from placing the bread in a basket while mentioning the animals separately?
answers: Only the animals are in the basket
The basket is for the bread, while the animals are brought separately
The bread may not be brought with the animals
questions.explanation: The bread is put in the basket, and the bull and rams are mentioned separately.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the preparations at the beginning of the first verse?
answers: To prepare an ordinary meal
To teach people how to raise cattle
To consecrate those appointed to minister to the Lord
questions.explanation: The preparations are for hallowing them to serve the Lord.

paragraphs.title: Washing and Clothing Aaron and His Sons

easy.question: Who was commanded to wash Aaron and his sons with water?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Aaron’s sons
easy.explanation: The command is given to Moses: he is to wash them with water.

easy.question: What was placed on Aaron’s turban?
answers: A sash
The holy crown
The breastplate
easy.explanation: The holy crown was placed on the turban.

easy.question: What garments were put on Aaron’s sons?
answers: A robe
A breastplate
Coats
easy.explanation: The verse says to put coats on Aaron’s sons.

medium.question: What happened first in the sequence?
answers: Aaron and his sons were washed with water
Oil was poured on Aaron’s head
Aaron’s sons were girded with sashes
medium.explanation: They were washed before Aaron was clothed and anointed.

medium.question: What does the phrase “gird him with the ephod’s skillfully woven band” mean?
answers: Remove the ephod
Fasten the ephod with its band
Place the ephod on his head
medium.explanation: The band was used to fasten or secure the ephod.

medium.question: What was the purpose of pouring anointing oil on Aaron’s head?
answers: To wash him
To decorate his turban
To anoint and consecrate him for his office
medium.explanation: The oil was used for his anointing and consecration.

challenge.question: What was placed directly on the turban rather than on Aaron’s head?
answers: The holy crown
The anointing oil
The ephod’s robe
challenge.explanation: The turban was put on his head, and the holy crown was placed on the turban.

challenge.question: Which detail is shared in the instructions for Aaron and his sons?
answers: Only Aaron is anointed with oil
They all wear priestly garments and sashes
They all receive a breastplate and holy crown
challenge.explanation: Aaron’s sons are clothed and girded, as part of their priestly service.

challenge.question: What does “consecrate Aaron and his sons” mean here?
answers: Fill their hands with water
Have them hold the priestly garments
Appoint and prepare them for priestly service
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes their preparation and appointment for priestly service.

questions.question: What was placed directly on the turban rather than on Aaron’s head?
answers: The holy crown
The anointing oil
The ephod’s robe
questions.explanation: The turban was put on his head, and the holy crown was placed on the turban.

questions.question: Which detail is shared in the instructions for Aaron and his sons?
answers: Only Aaron is anointed with oil
They all wear priestly garments and sashes
They all receive a breastplate and holy crown
questions.explanation: Aaron’s sons are clothed and girded, as part of their priestly service.

questions.question: What does “consecrate Aaron and his sons” mean here?
answers: Fill their hands with water
Have them hold the priestly garments
Appoint and prepare them for priestly service
questions.explanation: The phrase describes their preparation and appointment for priestly service.

paragraphs.title: The Bull as a Sin Offering

easy.question: Which animal was offered at the beginning of this passage?
answers: A bull
A lamb
A goat
easy.explanation: Verse 10 commands that the bull be brought.

easy.question: Who laid their hands on the bull’s head?
answers: Moses and the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
The priests alone
easy.explanation: Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the bull.

easy.question: Where was the bull killed?
answers: Outside the camp
Inside the Most Holy Place
Before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting
easy.explanation: The bull was killed before the Lord at the tent’s entrance.

medium.question: What happened after Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the bull?
answers: The bull was killed
The bull was released
The bull was returned to the camp
medium.explanation: Moses was then commanded to kill the bull.

medium.question: What does “base” mean in “the base of the altar”?
answers: The roof of the altar
The foundation or bottom of the altar
A tool used with the altar
medium.explanation: The blood was poured beside the lower part of the altar.

medium.question: Which part of the bull was burned, and what happened to the rest?
answers: Only the skin was burned and the rest was eaten
The entire bull was burned on the altar
The fat was burned, while the flesh, skin, and dung were burned outside the camp
medium.explanation: The fat was burned on the altar; the remaining parts were burned outside the camp.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from laying hands on the bull before it was killed?
answers: It created a symbolic connection between Aaron, his sons, and the offering
The bull became their private property
The bull was given permission to enter the camp
challenge.explanation: Laying hands expressed identification with the sacrifice.

challenge.question: What does the division of the blood between the altar’s horns and its base show?
answers: The blood was poured only on the ground
The blood had different prescribed places of application
The blood could not be used at all
challenge.explanation: The verse assigns the blood to the horns and the remainder to the altar’s base.

challenge.question: What do “it is a sin offering” and burning the remains outside the camp indicate?
answers: It was a thanksgiving offering eaten by the people
It was only for cleaning the altar
It was a sin offering whose remaining parts received special treatment outside the camp
challenge.explanation: The designation and disposal of the remains identify the offering as a sin offering.

questions.question: What can be inferred from laying hands on the bull before it was killed?
answers: It created a symbolic connection between Aaron, his sons, and the offering
The bull became their private property
The bull was given permission to enter the camp
questions.explanation: Laying hands expressed identification with the sacrifice.

questions.question: What does the division of the blood between the altar’s horns and its base show?
answers: The blood was poured only on the ground
The blood had different prescribed places of application
The blood could not be used at all
questions.explanation: The verse assigns the blood to the horns and the remainder to the altar’s base.

questions.question: What do “it is a sin offering” and burning the remains outside the camp indicate?
answers: It was a thanksgiving offering eaten by the people
It was only for cleaning the altar
It was a sin offering whose remaining parts received special treatment outside the camp
questions.explanation: The designation and disposal of the remains identify the offering as a sin offering.

easy.question: What did Aaron and his sons do before the ram was killed?
answers: They laid their hands on its head
They washed its entrails
They burned it
easy.explanation: They laid their hands on the ram’s head.

easy.question: What was done with the ram’s blood?
answers: It was poured outside the camp
It was sprinkled around the altar
It was smeared on the priests
easy.explanation: The blood was sprinkled around the altar.

easy.question: What was finally done with the entire ram?
answers: It was buried
It was given to Aaron
It was burned on the altar
easy.explanation: The whole ram was burned on the altar.

medium.question: What happened immediately after the ram was killed?
answers: Its blood was taken and sprinkled around the altar
Its entrails were washed
The entire ram was burned
medium.explanation: The blood was taken and sprinkled after the killing.

medium.question: What does “cut the ram in pieces” mean?
answers: Count the ram
Divide the ram into sections
Release the ram
medium.explanation: The ram was divided into its parts.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Burning, killing, and sprinkling blood
Washing, burning, and laying hands
Laying hands, killing, sprinkling blood, and burning
medium.explanation: The actions occur in that order.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the entire ram, not merely part of it, was offered?
answers: The words “the whole ram”
The words “on the head of the ram”
The word “around”
challenge.explanation: “The whole ram” emphasizes that all of it was burned.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from laying hands on the ram before its slaughter?
answers: The ram was meant to remain alive
It was a ritual act linking the offerers to the sacrifice
The ram was Aaron’s private property
challenge.explanation: The act symbolized the offerers’ connection with the sacrifice.

challenge.question: What does “a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto the Lord” indicate?
answers: The ram was prepared as an ordinary meal
The smoke had an unpleasant smell
The burning was an acceptable offering before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the ram as an offering pleasing to the Lord.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the entire ram, not merely part of it, was offered?
answers: The words “the whole ram”
The words “on the head of the ram”
The word “around”
questions.explanation: “The whole ram” emphasizes that all of it was burned.

questions.question: What can be inferred from laying hands on the ram before its slaughter?
answers: The ram was meant to remain alive
It was a ritual act linking the offerers to the sacrifice
The ram was Aaron’s private property
questions.explanation: The act symbolized the offerers’ connection with the sacrifice.

questions.question: What does “a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto the Lord” indicate?
answers: The ram was prepared as an ordinary meal
The smoke had an unpleasant smell
The burning was an acceptable offering before the Lord
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the ram as an offering pleasing to the Lord.

paragraphs.title: Consecrating the Priests with the Ram’s Blood

easy.question: What was taken at the beginning of verse 19?
answers: The other ram
Anointing oil
The priests’ garments
easy.explanation: The verse begins by commanding Moses to take the other ram.

easy.question: Who laid their hands on the ram’s head?
answers: Moses and the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
The priests alone
easy.explanation: Aaron and his sons laid their hands on it.

easy.question: Where was the ram’s blood sprinkled?
answers: On Aaron’s garments
On the sons’ ears
Around the altar
easy.explanation: The blood was sprinkled around the altar.

medium.question: Which happened first: laying hands on the ram or killing it?
answers: Laying hands on it
Killing the ram
They happened simultaneously
medium.explanation: Aaron and his sons laid hands on it before it was killed.

medium.question: What does “the tip of the ear” refer to?
answers: The hair on the head
The lower or projecting part of the ear
The skin on the hand
medium.explanation: It refers to the ear’s lower or projecting part.

medium.question: What was done after blood from the altar and anointing oil were taken?
answers: The ram was killed
They were placed on the ram’s head
They were sprinkled on Aaron, his sons, and their garments
medium.explanation: The blood and oil were sprinkled on the priests and their garments.

challenge.question: On which right-side body parts was the blood placed?
answers: Ear, hand, and foot
Eye, shoulder, and knee
Mouth, chest, and back
challenge.explanation: It was placed on the right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.

challenge.question: Who were consecrated together with their garments?
answers: Moses and the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
The ram and the altar vessels
challenge.explanation: Aaron, his sons, and their garments were consecrated.

challenge.question: What was the result of sprinkling the blood and oil on them and their garments?
answers: They returned home
They offered another ram
They and their garments were consecrated
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says they were made holy.

questions.question: On which right-side body parts was the blood placed?
answers: Ear, hand, and foot
Eye, shoulder, and knee
Mouth, chest, and back
questions.explanation: It was placed on the right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.

questions.question: Who were consecrated together with their garments?
answers: Moses and the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
The ram and the altar vessels
questions.explanation: Aaron, his sons, and their garments were consecrated.

questions.question: What was the result of sprinkling the blood and oil on them and their garments?
answers: They returned home
They offered another ram
They and their garments were consecrated
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says they were made holy.

paragraphs.title: The Wave Offering of the Ram and Bread

easy.question: What was taken from the ram?
answers: Fat portions and the right shoulder
Only the ram’s head
Only the ram’s skin
easy.explanation: The listed fat portions and right shoulder were taken.

easy.question: On whose hands were these things placed?
answers: On the altar only
On Aaron’s and his sons’ hands
On Moses’ hands alone
easy.explanation: They were placed in the hands of Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Why were these things burned on the altar?
answers: To distribute them to the people
To save them for the next day
As a sweet savor before the Lord
easy.explanation: They were burned as a pleasing offering before the Lord.

medium.question: What happened after everything was placed in Aaron’s and his sons’ hands?
answers: They waved it before the Lord
They distributed it to the people
They returned it to the basket
medium.explanation: They waved the items as a wave offering before the Lord.

medium.question: What does “wave offering” describe?
answers: Hiding the offering from the public
Moving or lifting the offering before the Lord
Eating it together
medium.explanation: It describes presenting the offering by waving it before the Lord.

medium.question: What was the main sequence in these verses?
answers: Burning, waving, then placing items in their hands
Distributing bread, eating, then burning
Placing items in their hands, waving, then burning
medium.explanation: The items were placed in their hands, waved, and then burned.

challenge.question: Which precise detail about the shoulder is given?
answers: The right shoulder
The left shoulder
Both shoulders
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically names the right shoulder.

challenge.question: What two kinds of things were placed in their hands?
answers: Only parts of the ram
Parts of the ram and kinds of bread from the basket
Only bread and oil
challenge.explanation: Parts of the ram and bread from the basket were placed in their hands.

challenge.question: What does “an offering made by fire unto the Lord” mean here?
answers: A woman serving in the sanctuary
A gift given to a poor person
An offering burned before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The context is an offering burned on the altar.

questions.question: Which precise detail about the shoulder is given?
answers: The right shoulder
The left shoulder
Both shoulders
questions.explanation: The verse specifically names the right shoulder.

questions.question: What two kinds of things were placed in their hands?
answers: Only parts of the ram
Parts of the ram and kinds of bread from the basket
Only bread and oil
questions.explanation: Parts of the ram and bread from the basket were placed in their hands.

questions.question: What does “an offering made by fire unto the Lord” mean here?
answers: A woman serving in the sanctuary
A gift given to a poor person
An offering burned before the Lord
questions.explanation: The context is an offering burned on the altar.

easy.question: What did Moses take from the ram of consecration?
answers: The breast
The shoulder
The head
easy.explanation: Moses was commanded to take the breast.

easy.question: Before whom was the breast waved?
answers: Before Aaron
Before the Lord
Before the Israelites
easy.explanation: It was waved as a wave offering before the Lord.

easy.question: To whom would the breast and shoulder belong permanently?
answers: Moses alone
All the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
easy.explanation: They were assigned to Aaron and his sons as a lasting statute.

medium.question: What was done with the breast after it was taken?
answers: It was burned immediately
It was waved before the Lord and became Moses’ portion
It was given to all Israel
medium.explanation: It was waved before the Lord and became Moses’ portion.

medium.question: What does “a statute forever” mean here?
answers: A one-time custom
A secret commandment
A permanent arrangement for future generations
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates a lasting arrangement.

medium.question: Why were the breast and shoulder given to Aaron and his sons?
answers: They were a contribution from the Israelites
They were Moses’ private property
They came from a foreign sanctuary
medium.explanation: They were an offering from the Israelites, from their peace offerings.

challenge.question: Which pair correctly describes the two parts and their actions?
answers: The breast was lifted and the shoulder was eaten
The breast was burned and the shoulder was waved
The breast was waved and the shoulder was lifted
challenge.explanation: The breast was a wave offering, and the shoulder was a heave offering.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “from the children of Israel”?
answers: The gift came from the people’s offerings, not a private source
The gift was given only by Aaron
The gift belonged to Israel’s king
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the offering came from the Israelites.

challenge.question: Which sequence matches the verses?
answers: Giving to Aaron, then taking, then waving
Taking the breast, waving it before the Lord, and establishing the gift for generations
Burning the breast, distributing the shoulder, then consecrating the priests
challenge.explanation: The breast is taken and waved, and the portions are then assigned permanently.

questions.question: Which pair correctly describes the two parts and their actions?
answers: The breast was lifted and the shoulder was eaten
The breast was burned and the shoulder was waved
The breast was waved and the shoulder was lifted
questions.explanation: The breast was a wave offering, and the shoulder was a heave offering.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “from the children of Israel”?
answers: The gift came from the people’s offerings, not a private source
The gift was given only by Aaron
The gift belonged to Israel’s king
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the offering came from the Israelites.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the verses?
answers: Giving to Aaron, then taking, then waving
Taking the breast, waving it before the Lord, and establishing the gift for generations
Burning the breast, distributing the shoulder, then consecrating the priests
questions.explanation: The breast is taken and waved, and the portions are then assigned permanently.

easy.question: To whom would Aaron’s holy garments belong after him?
answers: His sons
The elders of Israel
All the people
easy.explanation: The garments would pass to Aaron’s sons.

easy.question: How many days would the priest wear the garments?
answers: Three days
Seven days
Forty days
easy.explanation: The priest would wear them for seven days.

easy.question: Where would the priest come to minister in the holy place?
answers: Mount Sinai
The camp of Israel
The tent of meeting
easy.explanation: He would come to the tent of meeting to minister.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the holy garments given to Aaron’s sons?
answers: Only to distinguish them from the people
To prepare and consecrate them for priestly service
To protect them in battle
medium.explanation: The garments were connected with anointing and consecration.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: The priest enters the tent, then receives garments
The priest ministers, then is chosen from Aaron’s sons
Aaron’s garments pass to his sons, and the priest wears them seven days
medium.explanation: The garments pass to Aaron’s successor, who wears them for seven days.

medium.question: What does “to consecrate them in them” mean?
answers: To dedicate and prepare them for their office
To fill their hands with objects
To wash their hands with the garments
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to dedication and preparation for priestly service.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the priest in his stead, from among his sons”?
answers: Anyone in Israel may become the next priest
The next priest must be Aaron himself
The priesthood passes to a son from Aaron’s family
challenge.explanation: The next priest is to come from Aaron’s sons.

challenge.question: What does the connection between the garments, anointing, and consecration show?
answers: The garments help consecrate the priests, not merely improve their appearance
The garments only protect the priest’s body
The garments hide the priest from the people
challenge.explanation: The garments are part of the consecration process.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the priest wearing the garments for seven days?
answers: He wears them only on the seventh day
There is a fixed period of preparation or consecration
He must wear them continuously for life
challenge.explanation: Seven days marks a structured period of preparation.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the priest in his stead, from among his sons”?
answers: Anyone in Israel may become the next priest
The next priest must be Aaron himself
The priesthood passes to a son from Aaron’s family
questions.explanation: The next priest is to come from Aaron’s sons.

questions.question: What does the connection between the garments, anointing, and consecration show?
answers: The garments help consecrate the priests, not merely improve their appearance
The garments only protect the priest’s body
The garments hide the priest from the people
questions.explanation: The garments are part of the consecration process.

questions.question: What can be understood from the priest wearing the garments for seven days?
answers: He wears them only on the seventh day
There is a fixed period of preparation or consecration
He must wear them continuously for life
questions.explanation: Seven days marks a structured period of preparation.

paragraphs.title: Eating the Ram of Consecration and Burning the Remainder

easy.question: Who ate the flesh of the ram of consecration?
answers: Aaron and his sons
All the Israelites
Moses alone
easy.explanation: Aaron and his sons were commanded to eat it.

easy.question: Where was the ram’s flesh to be boiled?
answers: In an ordinary house
In a holy place
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: It was to be boiled in a holy place.

easy.question: What was done with flesh and bread left until morning?
answers: They were saved for the next day
They were given to strangers
They were burned with fire
easy.explanation: Anything remaining until morning was burned.

medium.question: Where did Aaron and his sons eat the flesh and bread?
answers: At Moses’ house
At the door of the tent of meeting
Inside the camp
medium.explanation: They ate them at the door of the tent of meeting.

medium.question: Why could a stranger not eat the flesh and bread?
answers: Because they were holy
Because they had not been cooked
Because they were intended for all the people
medium.explanation: The verse says a stranger may not eat them because they are holy.

medium.question: What does “if any of the flesh remains” mean?
answers: It must be burned immediately
A stranger may eat it
It is left over and not eaten
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to food remaining uneaten until morning.

challenge.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Boil, eat, and burn any leftovers
Burn, boil, and eat
Eat, save the leftovers, and boil them again
challenge.explanation: The flesh is boiled, eaten, and any remainder is burned.

challenge.question: What does eating the offering “to consecrate and to sanctify them” show?
answers: It was only an ordinary meal
The eating was part of their consecration
They ate in place of all Israel
challenge.explanation: The meal was part of the priests’ consecration.

challenge.question: What does “a stranger” mean in this context?
answers: Someone from a distant country
Someone who arrived late
Someone outside Aaron’s consecrated priestly group
challenge.explanation: The prohibition applies to one who does not belong to the consecrated group.

questions.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Boil, eat, and burn any leftovers
Burn, boil, and eat
Eat, save the leftovers, and boil them again
questions.explanation: The flesh is boiled, eaten, and any remainder is burned.

questions.question: What does eating the offering “to consecrate and to sanctify them” show?
answers: It was only an ordinary meal
The eating was part of their consecration
They ate in place of all Israel
questions.explanation: The meal was part of the priests’ consecration.

questions.question: What does “a stranger” mean in this context?
answers: Someone from a distant country
Someone who arrived late
Someone outside Aaron’s consecrated priestly group
questions.explanation: The prohibition applies to one who does not belong to the consecrated group.

paragraphs.title: Seven Days of Consecrating the Priests and Altar

easy.question: How many days were Aaron and his sons to be consecrated?
answers: Seven days
One day
Thirty days
easy.explanation: Their consecration lasted seven days.

easy.question: For whom were these instructions carried out?
answers: Moses and the elders
Aaron and his sons
All the Israelites
easy.explanation: The instructions begin, “Thus shalt thou do unto Aaron, and to his sons.”

easy.question: What offering was made each day?
answers: A thanksgiving ram
A peace-offering lamb
A bullock for a sin offering
easy.explanation: A bullock was offered each day as a sin offering.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the sin offering on the altar?
answers: To make atonement and cleanse the altar
To feed the priests
To mark the end of the festival
medium.explanation: The offering made atonement for and cleansed the altar.

medium.question: What does “make an atonement” mean here?
answers: Sing songs and pray
Make atonement and cleanse from sin
Give gifts to the priests
medium.explanation: The context concerns atonement and cleansing from sin.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: The altar becomes most holy, then offerings begin
Aaron is anointed, then the altar is built
The altar is cleansed and consecrated, then becomes most holy
medium.explanation: The altar is atoned for, anointed, and sanctified over seven days.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “whatever touches the altar shall be holy”?
answers: Contact with the altar brings the object into a holy status
No one may approach the altar
Only the high priest may touch the altar
challenge.explanation: The statement describes the holiness conveyed by contact, not a prohibition against approach.

challenge.question: What do the consecration of Aaron’s sons and the sanctification of the altar have in common?
answers: Both use only a bullock for a sin offering
Both continue for seven days
Both occur only after Israel enters the land
challenge.explanation: Both processes are explicitly said to last seven days.

challenge.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the consecration of the priests and the altar?
answers: Only the priests receive atonement, and the altar is merely anointed
The priests become most holy, and the altar receives special garments
Aaron’s sons are consecrated, while the altar is atoned for, anointed, and sanctified
challenge.explanation: The verses assign consecration to the priests and atonement, anointing, and sanctification to the altar.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “whatever touches the altar shall be holy”?
answers: Contact with the altar brings the object into a holy status
No one may approach the altar
Only the high priest may touch the altar
questions.explanation: The statement describes the holiness conveyed by contact, not a prohibition against approach.

questions.question: What do the consecration of Aaron’s sons and the sanctification of the altar have in common?
answers: Both use only a bullock for a sin offering
Both continue for seven days
Both occur only after Israel enters the land
questions.explanation: Both processes are explicitly said to last seven days.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the consecration of the priests and the altar?
answers: Only the priests receive atonement, and the altar is merely anointed
The priests become most holy, and the altar receives special garments
Aaron’s sons are consecrated, while the altar is atoned for, anointed, and sanctified
questions.explanation: The verses assign consecration to the priests and atonement, anointing, and sanctification to the altar.

paragraphs.title: The Daily Offering Morning and Evening

easy.question: How many one-year-old lambs were offered each day?
answers: Two
Three
One
easy.explanation: The command is for two lambs each day.

easy.question: When was the first lamb offered?
answers: At night
In the morning
At noon
easy.explanation: One lamb was offered in the morning.

easy.question: What was offered with the lamb?
answers: Wine only
Oil only
Fine flour, oil, and wine
easy.explanation: The offering included flour mixed with oil and a drink offering of wine.

medium.question: Why are the lambs called a continual offering?
answers: They were offered only on festivals
They were offered regularly every day
They were offered only when it rained
medium.explanation: “Continual” indicates a regular daily offering.

medium.question: What was the daily sequence?
answers: The second lamb in the morning and the first in the evening
Both lambs together in the morning
One lamb in the morning and the second at evening
medium.explanation: One was offered in the morning and the other at evening.

medium.question: What is a tenth deal in “a tenth deal of flour”?
answers: A measure of flour
A tool for lighting a fire
A type of lamb
medium.explanation: It is a specified measure of flour.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the second lamb’s offering being “according to the meat offering of the morning”?
answers: The second lamb needs no flour or drink offering
The evening offering is completely different
The second lamb receives the same accompanying offerings as the morning lamb
challenge.explanation: The evening lamb’s grain and drink offerings follow the morning pattern.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the service involved more than offering a lamb?
answers: The command to bring flour, oil, and wine
The command to offer one-year-old lambs
The command to offer two lambs per day
challenge.explanation: The flour, oil, and wine were additional offerings.

challenge.question: What is the central idea of verses 38–41?
answers: A one-time offering for a special event
A regular sacrifice performed twice each day
An offering made only during war
challenge.explanation: Two lambs were offered daily, one morning and one evening, with grain and drink offerings.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the second lamb’s offering being “according to the meat offering of the morning”?
answers: The second lamb needs no flour or drink offering
The evening offering is completely different
The second lamb receives the same accompanying offerings as the morning lamb
questions.explanation: The evening lamb’s grain and drink offerings follow the morning pattern.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the service involved more than offering a lamb?
answers: The command to bring flour, oil, and wine
The command to offer one-year-old lambs
The command to offer two lambs per day
questions.explanation: The flour, oil, and wine were additional offerings.

questions.question: What is the central idea of verses 38–41?
answers: A one-time offering for a special event
A regular sacrifice performed twice each day
An offering made only during war
questions.explanation: Two lambs were offered daily, one morning and one evening, with grain and drink offerings.

paragraphs.title: The Tent of Meeting as a Place of Encounter

easy.question: What kind of offering is mentioned?
answers: A continual burnt offering
A sin offering
A grain offering
easy.explanation: The verse begins with the continual burnt offering.

easy.question: Where was the continual burnt offering made?
answers: Inside the camp
At the entrance of the tent of meeting
On Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: It was offered at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

easy.question: With whom did the Lord say He would meet there?
answers: The Egyptians
The priests only
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The Lord would meet with the children of Israel there.

medium.question: What does “throughout your generations” show about the continual offering?
answers: It was to continue for many generations
It was offered only once
It belonged only to the wilderness generation
medium.explanation: The command was intended for future generations.

medium.question: What does “I will meet you there” mean?
answers: I will punish you there
I will meet with you there
I will send you away from there
medium.explanation: The Lord promises to meet with Israel at the tent.

medium.question: Which sequence fits the verses?
answers: The Lord sanctifies the place, then the offering is commanded, then Israel arrives
Israel leaves, Moses offers, and the Lord speaks elsewhere
The continual offering is made, the Lord meets and speaks there, and the place is sanctified by His glory
medium.explanation: The verses connect the offering, divine meeting, speech, and sanctification.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the mention of speaking to Moses and meeting with Israel?
answers: The tent is a place of connection between the Lord, Moses, and Israel
Only Moses is connected with the tent’s service
The Lord speaks to Moses somewhere else
challenge.explanation: The tent is described as a meeting place for the Lord, Moses, and Israel.

challenge.question: What does “the tabernacle shall be sanctified by my glory” mean?
answers: It becomes holy through decoration alone
The Lord’s glory makes the place holy
Israel sanctifies it without the Lord’s presence
challenge.explanation: The verse links the sanctuary’s holiness to the Lord’s glory.

challenge.question: Why mention both “the entrance of the tent” and “before the Lord”?
answers: To identify two separate offering sites
To show that the offering was only for Moses
To identify both the physical location and its presentation before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The first phrase gives the location; the second emphasizes the offering’s divine setting.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of speaking to Moses and meeting with Israel?
answers: The tent is a place of connection between the Lord, Moses, and Israel
Only Moses is connected with the tent’s service
The Lord speaks to Moses somewhere else
questions.explanation: The tent is described as a meeting place for the Lord, Moses, and Israel.

questions.question: What does “the tabernacle shall be sanctified by my glory” mean?
answers: It becomes holy through decoration alone
The Lord’s glory makes the place holy
Israel sanctifies it without the Lord’s presence
questions.explanation: The verse links the sanctuary’s holiness to the Lord’s glory.

questions.question: Why mention both “the entrance of the tent” and “before the Lord”?
answers: To identify two separate offering sites
To show that the offering was only for Moses
To identify both the physical location and its presentation before the Lord
questions.explanation: The first phrase gives the location; the second emphasizes the offering’s divine setting.

easy.question: Whom would the Lord sanctify to minister as priests?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses and his sons
All the kings of Israel
easy.explanation: The Lord would sanctify Aaron and his sons for priestly service.

easy.question: Where did the Lord promise to dwell?
answers: Among the children of Israel
In Egypt
Only on Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will dwell among the children of Israel.

easy.question: What would the Israelites know?
answers: That they would build new cities
That the Lord was their God who brought them out of Egypt
That Aaron would be their king
easy.explanation: They would know that the Lord brought them out of Egypt and was their God.

medium.question: What is the connection between sanctifying Aaron and his sons and their role?
answers: Their consecration prepares them to minister to the Lord
Their consecration makes them kings of Israel
Their consecration allows them to leave the tabernacle
medium.explanation: They are sanctified in order to serve as priests.

medium.question: What does “that I may dwell among them” mean?
answers: So that I may dwell and be present among them
So that I may send them into exile
So that I may hide the tabernacle from them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the Lord’s presence among Israel.

medium.question: Which sequence of ideas appears in these verses?
answers: The Exodus, construction of the altar, and selection of Aaron
Consecration of the sanctuary and priests, the Lord’s presence, and Israel’s recognition of Him
Israel recognizes the Lord, then leaves Egypt, then He dwells among them
medium.explanation: The verses move from consecration to divine presence and Israel’s knowledge of the Lord.

challenge.question: What deeper purpose of the Exodus is given in verse 46?
answers: To bring Israel into a relationship with the Lord dwelling among them
To make Israel wealthy
To keep Israel away from every holy place
challenge.explanation: The Lord brought Israel from Egypt so that He could dwell among them.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the relationship between the Lord and Israel involves identity and belonging?
answers: Mention of the tent alone
The statement, “I will be their God”
Mention of Aaron’s sons alone
challenge.explanation: “I will be their God” expresses a relationship of belonging, not merely presence.

challenge.question: What does the repeated statement “I am the Lord their God” emphasize?
answers: The Lord’s identity and His special relationship with Israel
That the verses concern only the priests
That the Lord is erasing the memory of the Exodus
challenge.explanation: The statement reinforces the Lord’s identity and covenant relationship with Israel.

answers: To bring Israel into a relationship with the Lord dwelling among them
To make Israel wealthy
To keep Israel away from every holy place
questions.explanation: The Lord brought Israel from Egypt so that He could dwell among them.
